advisories.title: Use the typed transaction query API instead of casting it to the root database
advisories.body: The double cast makes the relation query appear to be the root `db` inside a transaction, so future changes to the transaction or query shape can silently escape TypeScript's checking. Read the latest version with `tx.select(...).from(...).where(...).orderBy(...).limit(1)` and insert with `tx.insert(...)`; this keeps both operations visibly bound to the same typed transaction.
evidence: Premise: lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:20 casts `tx` through `unknown` to `typeof db` before querying → Improvement: retain compile-time transaction-bound query types → Fix: replace the relation query and cast with a direct `tx.select` query for the latest version.
lib/documents/issued-documents.ts:19-38 → the advisory lock, latest-version read, and insert are intended to run in the same transaction.

suppressions.candidate: Reformat or hand-simplify generated Drizzle snapshot metadata
suppressions.note: The snapshot is Drizzle-generated migration metadata; schema and SQL are the maintainable sources reviewed elsewhere.

suppressions.candidate: Change generated journal entry layout or timestamp
suppressions.note: The journal entry is generated migration bookkeeping and matches migration index 0006.

suppressions.candidate: Enforce append-only observations with database-level mutation prevention
suppressions.note: No application caller in the inspected checkout updates or deletes observations; a database trigger would be a separate policy design rather than a bounded local polish change.

suppressions.candidate: Retain the temporary scholarship upload feature flag
suppressions.note: The implementation contract explicitly makes the enabled upload path the only supported behavior and removes the temporary gate.

suppressions.candidate: Replace the embedded image payload with an independently optimized asset
suppressions.note: The executable asset is an exact copy of the approved Open Design master, as required by the technical specification; altering it would require a separate approval of the brand asset.
